buyer_added_terms.text: Buyer uploaded ATC document Click here to view the file. 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 1 Every establishment has its own locational constraints, topographic requirements, and law & ord er scenarios. Security deployment should be planned according to local needs and norms. The concerned POWERGRID official must be part of the security deployment plan. 2 Security personnel should patrol designated pathways at least 2–3 times during both day and nig ht. 3 The maximum tenure of a security guard at any POWERGRID location should be limited to 4 year s to avoid complacency. 4 When a new security agency takes over, security guards from the previous agency should not co ntinue with the new agency, as long association may lead to complacency and possible leakage of sensitiv e information. 5 Security guards deployed should preferably be not more than 55 years of age and should have a n ex-army or paramilitary background. 6 Regular training and fitness programs for security guards should be conducted quarterly, includin g jogging, push-ups, weapon handling, etc., followed by fitness tests. 7 Quarterly mock drills should be conducted under simulated conditions such as fire incidents or ca tching burglars/thieves red-handed. SOPs should be documented and available at strategic locations. 8 Adequate availability of batons, torches, whistles, umbrellas, and raincoats must be ensured thro ugh the contracting agency. 9 The deployment location of each security guard should be clearly defined within the substation p remises. 10 All security guards must have the contact details of the nearest police station and fire brigade, inc luding the name of the contact person, saved in their mobile phones. 11 Surprise checks should be conducted periodically to verify the readiness and availability of securit y guards at their assigned positions. 12 Quarterly meetings with the owner of the security agency should be conducted, with a feedback mechanism in place. Minutes of the meeting should be recorded. 13 If an employee is going out of station, a protocol should be established for informing Security and the Station In-Charge. Increased patrolling of the employee’s residence should be carried out during the pe riod of absence. .
